lesson.summary: Introduction to C: History, Characteristics and Classification
points: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in the early 1970s, building on B in the Unix environment.
C is general purpose, procedural and imperative; it is normally compiled.
Portability needs care with implementation-dependent behavior. Middle-level is an informal classroom label, not an ISO language category.

archive_evidence.history: Ritchie suggests that special memory cells on the PDP-7 may have inspired the increment operator. B already had that operator before the PDP-11 arrived.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: C's include mechanism made it possible to reuse declarations across source files. Functions in a library can be declared in one shared header.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: Imperative code gives instructions that can change program state. An assignment stores a new value. Later instructions read the state left by the earlier ones.
archive_evidence.source: GNU C Language Introduction and Reference Manual

archive_evidence.history: Printing a value before incrementing it can show a different number from printing after the increment. Trace the steps in their execution order.
archive_evidence.source: GNU C Language Introduction and Reference Manual

archive_evidence.history: An assignment changes the value stored in a variable. An equality test compares two values and can guide what instruction happens next.
archive_evidence.source: GNU C Language Introduction and Reference Manual
